messages:
alex: Heads-up: after yesterday's routing tweak we started getting cross-tenant egress fallbacks out of eu-west, latency and bills spiking. Anyone on call saw this too?
maya: saw the spike at ~04:10 UTC, tail latency for some dedicated tenants up ~120ms, and daily egress $ jumped ~30% for eu-west bucket
ton y: (typo) logs point at proxy failover to us-west for a bunch of euw allocations — NAT port exhaustion looks likely on the euw edge
kris: reverting the routing change would stop the fallbacks but cause a big reshuffle across dedicated slices. That churn could break warm pools for a while
alex: can we contain the damage without full revert? maybe per-tenant throttle or temporary hard cap for noisy ones
maya: quick data pull from ops-bot shows top egress users in the window: tenant-alpha 42GB, tenant-beta 30GB, tenant-gamma 28GB
ops-bot: query result -> top_tenants_by_egress: [tenant-alpha, tenant-beta, tenant-gamma, tenant-delta, tenant-epsilon]
maya: I also ran: rboxctl routes show --region=euw --filter=fallback=true and got ~180 fallback entries to usw1 over last 2h
ton y: option list: 1) immediate revert (churn risk) 2) soft-isolation caps on top-N tenants 3) expand NAT pool (infra change, takes time) 4) targeted egress throttling at proxy level
kris: expanding NAT pools has lead time and hardware ops. Soft caps look fastest and lowest blast radius if we accept short cold-starts for prewarmed traffic
alex: cost tradeoff numbers? if we cap top3 to 10MB/s what's estimated savings vs cold-start penalty?
kris: quick napkin: capping top3 saves ~18% of the egress surge. Prewarm miss overhead on requests ~2-3% additional infra cost (mostly transient)
ton y: I have a tiny patch for scheduler to enforce iso-soft-top3 (non-blocking token-bucket per-tenant). Risk: momentary increased tail for prewarm clients but avoids cross-region egress
maya: alright, i'll canary the iso-soft-top3 feature gate at 10% of eu-west allocations now. ops-bot, kick the deploy please
ops-bot: deploy job started -> iso-soft-top3 canary id d7f9a. Rolling to 10% euw as requested
maya: canary ran for 12m, no regressions in metrics for canary tenants. latency normalized for those we capped. rolling to 100% in 5m
ton y: monitoring shows egress volume trending down and cost spike flattening. Good signal
alex: nice work. let's avoid revert for now. kris, can you schedule a retro with billing/product to decide long-term tenant caps vs SLAs
kris: will do, add notes about NAT capacity and a follow-up plan to increase nat headroom in euw1 next maintenance window
alex: thanks everyone. keeping thread open for any rollbacks or regressions.
